chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who had a wife who had purified herself from her menstruation, so he went to a group of people and said, 'So-and-so is divorced.' Does the divorce take effect even though he did not say, 'Bear witness'? He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan (Imam al-Rida, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Does a divorce take effect if the husband says 'you are divorced' in front of witnesses but does not explicitly say 'bear witness'?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Shia juristic position that the mere presence of witnesses is sufficient for the validity of *talaq*, rendering the specific verbal formula of 'bearing witness' (*ishhad*) optional rather than mandatory. It highlights the pragmatic approach of the Imams in validating marital status changes based on the clear intent and public declaration of the husband, even if the technical ritualistic phrasing is omitted.
